tickets.title: Write the Stage 0 hypothesis and kill criteria, and commit them
tickets.description: State the falsifiable hypothesis (3-8s fights, 2-3 hits either way, committed attacks produce tension PROVIDED wind-ups are readable) and the symptom-to-diagnosis table, before building. Doc 18, Stage 0.

tickets.title: Character controller and camera rig
tickets.description: Movement, camera, traversal basics in a grey box. No enemies, no art. Ugly and playable by day 4. Doc 18, Stage 0.

tickets.title: Melee weapon class with committed attacks
tickets.description: Spear and shield. Light and heavy attack, commit with no cancel. Real wind-ups (0.35s / 0.7s) and recovery (0.4s / 0.8s) - the timing is the one thing that cannot be placeholdered. Doc 05.

tickets.title: Stamina governing attack, sprint and block
tickets.description: Pool 100; light 20, heavy 35, dodge 25; regen 25/s after 1s idle; block absorbs damage as stamina at 40%. Doc 18, starting numbers.

tickets.title: Block and dodge with no invincibility frames
tickets.description: Dodge is a committed movement burst, not a phase-through - this makes spacing the entire skill and is the riskiest single decision in Stage 0. First suspect if the prototype reads unfair while telegraphs are clean. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Poise and stagger economy
tickets.description: Stagger is the currency of melee - winning is about who gets interrupted, not who has more HP. Doc 05.

tickets.title: Audio telegraphs for every attack wind-up
tickets.description: Three distinct wind-up sounds from a library. Half the readability variable, and readability is the named confound in the hypothesis - not polish. Doc 12.

tickets.title: Skirmisher enemy state machine
tickets.description: Eight states - Unaware, Approach, Neutral, Tell, Commit, Punish, Rest, Stagger/Dead - as a C++ enum and switch on the pawn, NOT a behaviour tree. Neutral is the most important state: tension lives there, and a fight with no neutral contains no decisions. Commit is driven by a desire accumulator rather than a timer, and a mandatory Rest every 3 commits or 6s is designed content, not missing behaviour. Doc 18, skirmisher spec.

tickets.title: Attack rotation clamp and anti-frustration rules
tickets.description: Clamp enemy rotation to 30 deg/s during wind-up and ZERO during active frames. With i-frames removed this clamp does all the fairness work i-frames would otherwise do, and getting it wrong will make Stage 0 read as a design failure when it is a tracking bug. Plus: never attack from off-screen without audio, no chaining into player stagger beyond one follow-up, and return to spacing before re-committing. Doc 18.

tickets.title: AI tuning knobs and always-on debug overlay
tickets.description: Six floats editable without recompiling - desireGainRate, preferredSpacing, restDuration, punishReactionTime, windupScale, trackingCapDegPerSec - matching exactly the variables the 200-fight protocol turns. Plus a permanent on-screen draw of state, desire, spacing, timers and tracking angle; you will read the overlay more than the code. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Fight instrumentation and death-cause classification
tickets.description: Log duration, HP remaining, damage taken, hits, whiffs, blocks, dodges, and time-to-retry. Classify every death: out of stamina, whiff-punished, cornered, mistimed block, off-screen, or COULD NOT READ THE TELEGRAPH. The distribution is the diagnosis and separates a design failure from a readability failure. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Record the first 20 fights
tickets.description: The only honest record of what learning the combat looks like, before you become an expert at a game nobody else has played. Doc 18.

tickets.title: 200-fight tuning protocol: one variable per session
tickets.description: Fights 1-20 are bug-fixing. Then change one variable, play 30 fights, log, stop. Never tune mid-session - feel is comparative and memory of the previous build is short. Doc 18.

tickets.title: STAGE 0 GATE: two outside testers, then write the verdict
tickets.description: Thirty minutes each, no help, watched. Do they die and immediately try again? Deliberately earlier than the slice-end playtest - discovering a frustrating core three months and a dungeon later is the expensive version of the same finding. Write the verdict down before you are tempted to reinterpret it. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Run single-player as a one-player listen server
tickets.description: First permanent code, AFTER the Stage 0 gate - Stage 0 is disposable and must not be slowed by architecture. The most important single architectural item; cannot be retrofitted. Doc 15.

tickets.title: Route all state mutation through an event/command layer
tickets.description: Event-sourced state everywhere, not just narrative facts. Prerequisite for co-op and the consequence ledger. Starts after the Stage 0 gate. Doc 15.

tickets.title: Eliminate singleton assumptions about 'the player'
tickets.description: Audio, streaming, encounter spawning and the Pressure must not be written against a single global pawn. Starts after the Stage 0 gate. Doc 15.

tickets.title: Write the one-page style guide and lock the snap grid
tickets.description: Palette, material value ranges, world scale rules, 2m or 4m snap grid, silhouette requirements, fog and grade defaults. First permanent-content decision, after the Stage 0 gate. Doc 16.

tickets.title: Rebuild the Stage 0 combat loop on the permanent architecture
tickets.description: Stage 0 is disposable by design, so the controller, combat kit and skirmisher are re-implemented on top of the listen server and event layer. Days rather than weeks, because by now you know exactly what you are building - but it is real work and was previously implied by doc 18 without a ticket. Doc 18, Stage 0 code is disposable.

tickets.title: Bow and the ranged-opening preparation loop
tickets.description: Melee-only tests half the identity. Open at range, finish in melee. Doc 18, scope.

tickets.title: Anchor enemy role
tickets.description: Slow, high poise, controls space. Tests the stagger economy. Doc 05.

tickets.title: Artillery enemy role
tickets.description: Ranged pressure, forces movement, dies fast when reached. Tests positioning and terrain use. Doc 05.

tickets.title: Enemy validation harness across five terrain conditions
tickets.description: Every enemy validated in open field, dense forest, narrow defile, steep slope, and shallow water. Steep slopes and water edges are where navmesh and root motion reliably fail. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Build the 500m test-fixture map
tickets.description: Hand-built, containing all five AI-breaking terrain conditions plus a ridge, a river, and 2-3 landmark silhouettes. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Ability system with swappable power source
tickets.description: One ability system; the Law axiom swaps only what pays for it. Ship the slice on Hecatomb (health is the offering, no extra HUD). Doc 05.

tickets.title: ARCHITECTURE TEST: implement The Last Favour power source
tickets.description: Second power source as finite charges. If this takes more than one day, the abstraction is wrong and two combat systems have been designed by accident. Doc 18.

tickets.title: Loot, consumables and encumbrance
tickets.description: Consumables, charges, 4-5 catalogue items, weight on. Encumbrance is not optional - scarcity is a primary question. Doc 06.

tickets.title: Merchant and repair services
tickets.description: One merchant, one repair. Durability as a repair cost, not breakage. Doc 06.

tickets.title: Discovery XP and the four stats
tickets.description: XP from reaching places and first-time events. Health, stamina, carry, attunement. No kill-XP, no use-based grinding. Doc 07.

tickets.title: Trainer with capability unlocks
tickets.description: One trainer, 4-5 discrete capability unlocks with no ranks. Doc 07.

tickets.title: Hand-build the regional-tier dungeon
tickets.description: ~15 minutes, authored layout, vertical structure and a shortcut back. Doc 09, regional tier.

tickets.title: Landmark navigation: compass, directions, no waypoints
tickets.description: No minimap, no quest pins. Compass bearing plus verbal directions against landmark silhouettes. Doc 11.

tickets.title: Minimal map screen
tickets.description: Functional but ugly. The hand-drawn diegetic map is an art investment and is deferred. Doc 13.

tickets.title: Art baseline: material clamp, colour grade, covered faces
tickets.description: Clamp roughness and specular ranges across all assets, establish one colour grade, use covered-face characters from day one. Doc 16.

tickets.title: SLICE GATE: outside playtest with five fresh players
tickets.description: Watch without helping. Count quits versus retries. Tension and frustration are indistinguishable from inside the project. Doc 18.
